links.note: Confluence as the meeting point of two or more rivers - the word appears in this concept, where a river's source and its confluence with other rivers are held sacred.
Mountains recognised by a broad base, steep slopes and a narrow summit, much higher than the surrounding landscape - this concept's definition, in exactly those three features.
Why some mountains are permanently snow-capped - this concept says that at high altitudes the snow may never melt. Already linked and correct.

Young against old mountains - this concept reads age off shape, tall sharp peaks like the Himalayas being relatively young and shorter rounded ones like the Aravalli much older, with the Himalayas still growing.
The vegetation of montane forests - this concept names the conifers, pines, firs, spruce and deodar, growing tall and cone-shaped with thin pointed leaves.
Why herding is often preferred over agriculture in mountainous regions - this concept gives the reason, rugged terrain and steep slopes limiting regular farming to some valleys.
Plateaus called storehouses of minerals, with gold and diamond on the East African Plateau and iron, coal and manganese in Chhota Nagpur. Already linked and correct.
What makes floodplains suitable for agriculture - rivers depositing particles of rock, sand and silt called sediments, making the soil very fertile. Already linked and correct.
Precipitation as water from the atmosphere reaching the ground in any form, most commonly rain, snow and hail - this concept's gloss. Already linked and correct.

How erosion wears mountains down over time - this concept explains that shorter and more rounded mountains like the Aravalli Range are much older, having been rounded by erosion, while upliftment and erosion both continue in the Himalayas.
Plains generally not more than 300 metres above sea level - that figure, which is the discriminating half of the comparison, is stated only in this concept's definition of plains.
The significance of sediments deposited by rivers in the plains - this concept explains that the deposits make the soil very fertile and the plains ideal for crops of all kinds.
Hot deserts like the Sahara and Thar against cold ones like the Gobi - this concept makes exactly that contrast with those examples. Already linked and correct.
Arunima Sinha, who lost a leg at 22 and climbed Everest in 2013 and then the highest peak of every continent - this concept's account of her. Already linked and correct.
Comparing the Himalayas with the Aravalli Range - this concept is where those two are set against each other, tall sharp peaks and still rising versus shorter, rounded and much older.

Plateaus as storehouses of minerals with Chhota Nagpur and the East African Plateau as the examples - the mineral half, which leads the question, is this concept's content. Already linked and defensible, so left alone.

How the tinai classification reflects an understanding of the environment - this concept says the five tinais are a different classification of landforms that reflect a keen awareness of diverse regions and the deep connection between humanity and the natural environment.
The Earth is my mother and I am her child - this concept opens the chapter on that line from the Bhumi Sukta of the Atharva Veda.
Kalidasa's description of the Himalayas - the two verses from the Kumarasambhava, where the Himalaya rises in the north like a living god, are quoted only in this concept.
Terrace farming as cutting steps into steep slopes, and why it suits mountainous regions - this concept defines it and gives the reason. Already linked and correct.

Rivers as the lifelines of plains, economically and culturally - this concept supplies both sides, river fishing, agriculture and irrigation and easy navigation on the one hand, and sacred sources and confluences with their festivals and rituals on the other.
The challenges faced by people in mountainous regions - this concept is the one that names and glosses flash flood, landslide, avalanche and cloudburst, which is the bulk of the answer.
Rivers forming waterfalls where they run off a plateau's steep side is this concept's explanation, and it names Victoria, Hundru, Jog and Nohkalikai. Already linked and defensible, so left alone.

The keyed sub-prompt asks which of the three major landforms the area represents, which is this concept's classification of landforms into mountains, plateaus and plains. Already linked and defensible, so left alone.
The densely populated Ganga plain, its fertility, pollution and groundwater depletion from irrigation - all four sub-prompts come from this concept. Already linked and correct.

The Thar community's folk songs and legends, migration with livestock and desert adaptation - this concept names the Thar as a hot desert, notes the rich cultural traditions of communities living in or migrating through it, and closes on human adaptability and resilience.
